messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, nothing’s breaking yet—but the cracks are there. The top’s holding for now, but it’s less about loyalty and more about fear of what happens if they don’t. The streets are quiet, but that’s not peace—it’s exhaustion. And the money? It’s moving where the regime can’t see it. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t know if it’s a storm or just more of the same. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 2: "*"Listen—this isn’t just another crackdown or a temporary squeeze. The cracks are spreading faster than they can paper over, and the fear that used to keep people quiet is turning into something else. The elites are circling the wagons, the soldiers are restless, and the money’s drying up—yet they’re still putting on a show. That’s not stability. That’s a house of cards waiting for the right gust. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. We need to be ready when the wind changes."*"
Sender 3: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards where half the deck’s already missing. People are moving, talking, testing… but no one’s sure which way it’ll fall. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your exits open—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they’re acting like they’ve got time. The inner circle’s even bringing in fresh blood, and the streets? People are still fixing up their homes, starting businesses—like they’re betting on the long game. But don’t get comfortable: the cracks are there if you know where to look. And those extra flights out of the capital? That’s not just business as usual."*"
Sender 5: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air, even if no one’s ready to name it yet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards where the wind’s picking up—no one knows if it’ll hold or collapse, but everyone’s holding their breath waiting to see which way it falls."*"
Sender 6: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the quiet of a ship drifting without a captain. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in plain sight: the soldiers aren’t even pretending to be alert, the elites are whispering about no one being in charge, and the only thing holding things together is bureaucracy and habit. The real question isn’t if something’s coming—it’s whether the pieces will fall apart before they can even try to stop it."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, it’s like we’re all holding our breath—no one’s running, but no one’s relaxing either. The regime’s tightening its grip, but the cracks are showing, and the jokes are getting sharper. Could go either way, but if it tips, it won’t be slow."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t just another wave of unrest. The regime’s showing cracks *everywhere*: soldiers are muttering, the elite are clinging to each other like drowning men, and even the kids in the streets are chanting what their parents taught them. The fear’s gone. The question now is whether the military’s silence means they’re waiting for the right moment—or if they’re just waiting to see who wins."*"
Sender 9: "*"Something’s shifting—less noise from the top, but the cracks are showing in the little things. The regime’s holding tight now, but the street’s getting louder, and the money’s slipping. If they can’t even pull off a census, what else is breaking behind the scenes? Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re still standing, but the cracks are showing—no panic in the ranks yet, but the clinic’s stocking up, the neighbors are watching the borders, and the vendors aren’t even flinching. Something’s coming, and it’s not just another purge. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see where the wind shifts first."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the cracks are showing—payments are late, the security forces are holding but the commanders are the wild card, and the regime’s grip is slipping even if they’re not admitting it. The mood on the street is angry, but we’re still too scattered to do anything about it yet. The question isn’t *if* things break, but *when*—and whether we’re ready when they do."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the regime’s acting like a boxer who’s taken too many hits but won’t drop—still swinging, but you can see the exhaustion. The streets feel like a held breath: no one’s running *toward* anything yet, but no one’s pretending everything’s fine either. The real question is whether this is a slow unraveling or just their way of tightening the screws before the next crackdown. Either way, we should assume the worst is still possible—and maybe closer than we think."*"
Sender 13: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The regime’s acting like it’s preparing for a long winter, not just another season of the same old cracks. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether they’ll do it fast or slow—and whether we’ll see it coming."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—meetings are falling apart, the army’s quiet, and even the courts are stalling. The regime’s losing its grip, but we don’t know yet if the security forces will turn on us or just let things burn. Stay sharp, stay ready, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s not as steady as they want us to think—patrols are avoiding trouble spots, the census got canceled last minute, and half the people we know are quietly packing go-bags while the other half are acting like nothing’s wrong. They’re holding on, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 16: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual cracks in the facade. The inner circle is fracturing, orders are being questioned, and even the shopkeepers are dropping their masks. The regime’s scrambling to control the narrative while the machine sputters—diplomats are bailing, logistics are stalling, and no one, *not even the usual sources*, knows what’s coming next. We need to be ready for anything."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing. The leadership’s still in sync, but it’s like a machine running too hot, and the military’s just going through the motions. The streets are patchy: some places feel like a spark could ignite it, others like nothing’s happening. The real question isn’t if they’re in trouble, but how long they can keep pretending they’re not."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are sweating—everyone can see it now, even the neighbors we’ve never spoken to before. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s shifting, and the question isn’t *if* something gives, just *when* and *who* gets left holding the pieces."*"
Sender 19: "*"Something’s shifting—fast. The elite are fracturing, the security forces are quietly stepping back, and even the usual enforcers are losing their nerve. The regime’s grip is slipping, but nobody knows yet if it’s the beginning of the end or just another false dawn. Stay sharp, stay safe, and keep your ears open—this could be the moment we’ve been waiting for."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—things are hanging by a thread right now. The regime’s still standing, but it’s all propped up with duct tape and nerves: payments are late, the security forces are hunkered down, and even the elites are whispering that one wrong move could send everything crashing. The streets are quiet, but not because people are happy—it’s like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the spark. And the regime knows it. That’s why they’re overcompensating with all this ‘normalcy’ noise. We’re in the eye of the storm, and I don’t know which way the wind will blow next."*"
Sender 21: "*"Listen—this isn’t just tension, it’s a powder keg with a flickering fuse. The elites are hedging, the military’s nerves are showing, and the streets are patchy but charged. If something sparks—anything—it could go either way fast. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We need to watch the gaps, not the headlines."*"
Sender 22: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air, like the quiet before a storm. The regime’s grip is tightening, but the cracks are showing, and the question isn’t *if* things will break, but *when* and *how hard*. Stay sharp, stay close, and trust your instincts—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 23: "*"The regime’s still holding on, but it’s like watching someone grip a rope that’s fraying—no one’s letting go yet, but you can feel the tension in every little shift. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but what happens when the first thread snaps—and whether we’re ready for it."*"
Sender 24: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping—small cracks, but they’re spreading. People are talking like it’s inevitable, not a question of if, and the security forces are already scrambling behind the scenes. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet after the storm’s already passed, and no one’s noticed yet. The regime’s playing dead, but the embassies know it, the money knows it, and soon the streets will too. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but the rules just changed."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
